subject: penguin
pitch: An emperor penguin chick's proud parent. Glossy blue-black back and head, a crisp white belly blending into a warm golden-yellow patch at the neck and ear, a long slender beak with an orange-pink stripe, stubby flippers held slightly out, and big black feet. A fluffy grey chick peeks out from between its feet.
reasoning:
I'm planning a TypeScript module using the builder API to create an emperor penguin scene, sizing the adult around 1 meter tall with a smaller fluffy grey chick near its feet at about 0.3 meters.

I'm sketching the body as a sweep or chain along a spine path from hips to head, working out how the knots and segment names should map so the torso shape comes out egg-like, with a root joint anchoring everything from the hips.

Chains are cleaner for rigging, so I'll keep role as "spine". For the body I'll sweep along the chain with a radius function varying by t — wider at the hips, tapering through the chest, narrowing at the neck, and rounding out slightly at the head, giving that classic rounded penguin silhouette.

I'll keep the head embedded in the neck sweep, with the head radius tapering to about 0.11 near the top, landing around 1.1m for an adult-scale figure. For coloring, I'm planning a paint function based on surface normals -- dark on the back-facing side, white on the belly, with a dark head and a golden ear/neck patch positioned near the side of the head.

Defining color constants now: navy-black for the back, off-white belly, gold patches, orange beak stripe, black beak and feet, and grey fluff for chicks. Writing paint function...

Still refining color zones...

Good, both are exported. For the flippers, I'm figuring out the best approach—stubby and held slightly out—considering a chain-based shape from shoulder going down and out, with a role like "arm" or "wing" for naming the flipper joints.

Actually I'll model each flipper as a flat slab (polygon-based plate) rooted to a shoulder joint, keeping its points in a constant-z plane so the normal faces outward and the thin dimension is along z. I'm positioning the left shoulder joint near the chest parent, defining it with b.joint and setting up the bone attachment for the flipper slab.

Since normals get computed via Newell's method, winding order from mirroring shouldn't actually matter—the frame adapts to face the right direction regardless. Now thinking about feet: big black webbed feet, maybe using the same slab approach or building legs as chains from the hips.

Keeping legs short and hidden, with feet as the visible part—maybe a capsule rod from hip to ankle, then extruding a flat three-toed outline pointing forward in the x-z plane for the foot shape.

I'm setting the foot's origin so outline points become offsets from the ankle joint, attaching the extrude to the "footL" bone at the ankle position. For now I'll keep the toe shape simple rather than webbed, then move on to defining the leg as a rod running from the hip down to the ankle joint.

Building the leg chain and sweep...

I'll use catmull for the spine chain, importing it from the builder's path exports, with knots at the key body points (hips, chest, neck, head), then sweep that chain with a radius function to build the body's smooth skin.

For the radius profile, I'm approximating arc-length positions with a piecewise function that's narrower at the hips, widest at the chest, and tapering toward the neck and head, since a penguin's body bulges mid-chest. For the head, rather than adding a separate sphere part, I'll just let the sweep's end radius form a rounded bulb shape.

Now I'm working out the beak: a slender tapered rod extending forward and slightly downward from the head, colored black with an orange-pink stripe along the lower mandible to mimic an emperor penguin's beak plate, using sector-based coloring and a tapering radius array from wider at the base to narrow at the tip.

I also realize the mouth should probably be split into separate upper and lower jaw joints so it can open properly, so I'm planning a "jaw" joint parented to the head, with the lower beak portion rigged to that jaw rather than fixed to the head itself.

Still placing beak coordinates...

I'll simplify: upper mandible solid black, lower mandible orange-pink, matching the classic Emperor penguin look rather than fussing with underside sectors.

For eyes, I'll add small dark spheres on either side of the head to represent the eyes, keeping the painted ear patch as is. Then I'll set up the shoulder joints and mirrored flipper positions for the flippers.

Now I need to work out the spine chain joint naming - "chest", "neck", "head" as spans along the path, with the root "hips" joint placed separately and each chain joint positioned at its corresponding parameter along the catmull path.

I'll rename the chain joints to torso, neck, head, skull, with skull as the tip at the top. I'll attach the beak and jaw to the skull joint near the top of the head instead of lower down to keep the anatomy cleaner.

Still working out beak geometry...

Now I'm thinking about adding a grey fluffy chick positioned between the penguin's feet, near the front below the breast, figuring out appropriate coordinates relative to the body and legs.

Adding the chick head with a small beak and eyes, then a few spike tufts for fluff on top, plus tiny black feet peeking out underneath.

All chick parts attach to a "chick" bone using sphere geometry, with solid grey color for simplicity rather than card-based texturing.

Adding tufts via small spikes placed around the sphere surface, computed from outward directions with jittered random positions, and setting up a paint function for body color blending based on position and normal.

Still writing paint logic...

Still refining color blend logic...

Now I'm defining the spine sweep with the body paint texture, then setting up the skeletal joints starting with the hips root and building a spine chain through torso, neck, head, and skull using a catmull curve.

Confirming path exports include catmull, then I'm defining a body sweep radius function that interpolates thickness at key points along the spine using a lerp helper over control pairs like (0, 0.15), (0.3, 0.2), (0.6, 0.19), tapering toward the tail.

Simplifying to just pass an evenly-spaced radius array for the sweep instead of custom keyed interpolation. Now I'm checking the leg and hip placement against the body bottom radius, realizing the body's hips need to sit low enough that the belly nearly touches the ground where the feet are, rather than floating above it.

I need to check whether path parameter t corresponds to arc-length fraction along the segments, since that affects how the radius values map to actual positions along the body.

I settle on radii values [0.15, 0.2, 0.2, 0.17, 0.1, 0.11] across the height, making sure the head sits properly at the top around y=1.11. Now I'm considering whether the penguin should use elliptical cross-sections instead, since penguins are flatter front-to-back than side-to-side, so I'd need separate rx and ry values at each height level.

Then I'm working out the flipper placement, estimating the body radius near the shoulder (around y=0.74) to be roughly 0.17-0.19, so I place the shoulder joint just outside that at x=0.15. I'm sketching out the flipper as a slab of points running from the shoulder down and outward, roughly [0.14,0.80], [0.22,0.72], [0.27,0.55], [0.25,0.42], [0.2,0.46], [0.14,0.62], forming a curved paddle shape.

Now I'm figuring out the joint hierarchy — deciding whether torso, neck, head, and skull-tip correspond to the catmull knot points at arc positions 0, 0.32, 0.6, and 1.0, and concluding the flipper's shoulder joint should just be parented under "neck" since the exact parent doesn't affect positioning much, only the transform chain. Moving on to the leg now.

I'm setting up the leg chain, rooting it under a "hips" joint and defining a two-span polyline path for "hipL" to "ankleL" with contact at the ankle, using a thin ink-colored sweep since polylines don't need catmull interpolation. For the foot, I'm sketching an extruded outline relative to the ankle bone, pointing forward with points forming a rounded heel-to-toe shape, though I'm reconsidering since a simple blob won't read as having distinct toes.

Writing foot outline points...

I'm checking the extrude parameters—confirming the x/y direction vectors are literal arrays, skipping smoothing since it could cause the concave toe shape to self-intersect, and using a small bevel instead. I'm positioning the foot so its bottom sits flush at y=0 for proper ground contact, placing it forward of the ankle so the heel sits near the leg and toes extend outward, sized generously to match an emperor penguin's proportionally large feet.

Now I'm placing the eyes as small dark spheres slightly embedded into the head sphere near the skull bone, and sketching the beak as a tapered black tube swept along a short polyline from the face outward, attached to the skull joint.

For the lower beak, I'm adding a jaw joint parented to the skull with a forward-facing direction, then sweeping a thinner tapered tube along it to form the mandible, considering an orange-pink tint for color variation on this lower piece.

I'll give the lower mandible an ink-black base color with orange sector stripes on both sides (symmetric sectors around the tube), keeping the upper beak solid black without any sectors. Next I'm setting up the chick joint parented to the hips.

For positioning, I'm checking whether the chick's sphere overlaps the parent body given their respective centers and radii, and deciding the chick should sit peeking out just in front of the feet at roughly [0, 0.11, 0.27]. I'm defining the chick as a small sphere geometry with modest segment counts for a simple rounded shape.

Now I'm adding the chick's head, a tiny orange beak cone rotated to point forward, and small dark eyes, then generating fuzzy tufts by scattering spikes evenly around the head using a golden-angle spherical distribution for natural-looking placement.

Explicitly tagging "chick" as the bone for proper weighting. For feet, I'll add small orange extrusions at the chick's base to suggest tiny webbed feet.

I'm reconsidering the chick's placement relative to the feet—since the feet extend forward to about z 0.16 and the chick sits further out at z 0.27, it's really in front rather than nestled between them. To match "peeks out from between its feet," I should reposition the chick closer in, tucked laterally between the feet instead.

Settling on positioning the chick at roughly [0, 0.11, 0.22] with its head slightly forward, nestled between the legs which sit at x ±0.08. I'm defining the chick as its own joint on the hips bone, giving it its own color distinct from the parent's body paint, and keeping the flippers held slightly out per the description. Wrapping up with the metadata export and the main build function that assembles the full rig and returns the baked root.

Writing imports and shoulder joints...

Feet extrude in INK, and the eyes are small spheres positioned near the skull tip, parented to the skull bone.

Now I'm figuring out placement for a golden neck patch — positioning it on the front-upper neck, roughly centered above the head joint.

Then I'm working out the ear patches, setting their centers near the top of the skull on each side and picking a matching radius so the painted color blends smoothly with the surface curvature at that height.

For the belly, I'm using a smoothstep transition on the y-coordinate so white fades in below the mid-body and stays off higher up, combined with a front-facing mask based on surface normal so the white only appears on the chest/belly side, keeping the back and head black.

Now I'm setting up the actual builder: creating the penguin chick entity, defining a hips joint as the root, then building a spine chain with catmull-rom control points running from hips through torso, neck, head, and skull. I'm sweeping a tapered body mesh along that spine with varying radii, then starting to set up the legs with a loop over left/right sides.

For each leg, I'm defining a three-joint chain (hip, knee, ankle) and realizing the names array needs three entries to properly capture the tip joint, then sweeping a thin cylindrical mesh along that chain to form the leg geometry.

Now I'm working on the feet—extruding a symmetric foot outline anchored to the ankle bone, with the foot shape defined as a small polygon of offset points in local x/z coordinates.

Then I'm moving on to shoulders and flippers, planning the flipper joint positions using a mirrored x-offset off the neck/shoulder bone.

Adding more slab calls...

Adding jaw joint and beak lower sweep...

Now setting up the chick joint attached to hips, and starting its body part as a sphere.

Checking the head position relative to the body — head centre at y 0.27 overlaps nicely with the body top around 0.21, so they should blend together without a visible gap.

Now I'm positioning the beak using a small rotated cone so its tip points forward from the face, placing the eyes as tiny black spheres just above and to the sides of the beak, then moving on to figuring out the feet placement beneath the body.

Setting feet thickness to reach top at 0.016 works fine, and since the feet already touch the ground at 0, the overall model stays grounded even if the sphere itself floats slightly — within acceptable tolerance.

Looping through spike tufts on the chick, I'm renaming variables to avoid clashing with the `paint` function, using grey for the chick body and gold accents around the ear area, then finalizing the color-mixing logic with properly typed RGB values before returning the completed model.
